Table of cross correlations X x Y (wide: one row per predictor, one column per score)

Source: R/tables.R
tbl_cor_cross.Rd

Same content and same colour scale as plot_cor_cross(). Binary predictors are grouped under "Binary 0/1" and carry a footnote.

Usage

tbl_cor_cross(
  x,
  labels = NULL,
  digits = 2,
  palette = COR_PAL,
  show_note = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  stub_label = "Predictor"
)

Arguments

x

output of cor_cross() or plot_cor_cross()

labels

named vector variable -> label (default: those given to cor_cross())

digits

decimals of the coefficients

palette

colours (named low / high); NULL = no colour

show_note

add the reading lines of binary variables

title, subtitle

override the automatic texts

stub_label

header of the row labels

Value

a gt_tbl

Examples

d  <- simulate_cor_data(150)
cc <- cor_cross(d, c("CRP", "IL6", "BIN_CRP"), c("depression", "fatigue"),
                covariates = "age", labels = attr(d, "labels"))
tbl_cor_cross(cc)

1 [0/1] binary: r_s ≈ Mann-Whitney (rank difference between groups); |r_s| ≤ √(3pq) ≤ 0.87, not comparable with continuous variables
    
Cells: r_s and stars; colour = same scale as the heatmap (blue < 0 < red). Confidence intervals: tbl_cor_long().
    
Adjusted p, Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) over the 3 predictors of each score (column): * < 0.05, ** < 0.01, *** < 0.001; no star = adjusted p ≥ 0.05.
    
Continuous: r_s = cov(rank_x, rank_y) / (SD(rank_x) × SD(rank_y)); partial: r_s,xy.z = r(e_x.z, e_y.z), residuals of the ranks on the k = 1 covariate terms z; t-test, n − 2 − k df.
    
Binary [0/1]: r_s = r_rb × √(3pq), r_rb = 2 AUC − 1 (rank-biserial, ≡ Mann-Whitney test), p, q = group proportions; |r_s| ≤ 0.87, not comparable with continuous pairs.
    
Notation: Makowski D, Ben-Shachar MS, Patil I, Lüdecke D (2020), J Open Source Softw 5(51):2306, doi:10.21105/joss.02306.
